messages.subject: auto.snapshot
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying out packrat for the first times. So apologies if this is cringeworthy newbie question. I did search for an answer first.

I have auto-snapshot turned on. But none of the installed packages have a value in the Packrat column in teh Rstudio Packages window yet. I worked for a few hours on it yesterday, and have saved files, git committed, close down Rstudio, and the PC overnight. Still not there now.

How long before this auto feature kicks in. It would be brilliant to be able to forget about it!

Thanks Simon

messages.subject: Re: auto.snapshot
messages.body_plain:
I'm guessing that the automatic snapshot is failing for the same reason that the manual snapshot is failing: the RDCOMClient package can't be located in an available repository.

Where was that package obtained from? If it's not available on any public repository (e.g. CRAN, BioC, GitHub) you might consider just ignoring it:

    packrat::opts$ignored.packages("RDCOMClient")

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.subject: Re: auto.snapshot
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

Darn -- it looks like the 'ignore' option isn't being properly respected here. :-/ I'll try to take some time to investigate.

Issue logged here: https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/issues/292

I just took some time to investigate, and it looks like RDCOMClient is a package distributed on omegahat -- you might need to add the associated repository, with e.g.

    packrat::add_repos(omegahat = "http://www.omegahat.net/R")

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.subject: Re: auto.snapshot
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

You likely need to use `options(pkgType = "source")` then -- it sounds like the omegahat mirrors don't distribute binaries for this package. (You will also need Rtools and potentially other external libraries to install this from source, unfortunately).

Kevin
